passages.text: The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD holds power over all people.
A king rules a nation.
A king’s heart guides his decisions.
The LORD holds the king’s heart in His hand.
The LORD controls the king’s heart like a stream of water.
The LORD directs the king’s heart wherever He wants.
The LORD chooses the king’s path.
The LORD’s will guides the king’s actions.
passages.original: פַּלְגֵי־ מַ֣יִם לֶב־ מֶ֭לֶךְ בְּיַד־ יְהוָ֑ה עַֽל־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֖ר יַחְפֹּ֣ץ יַטֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: All a man’s ways seem right to him, but the LORD weighs the heart.
passages.sermon: Every person thinks his own way is right.\r\nThe LORD examines each person’s heart.
passages.original: כָּֽל־ דֶּרֶךְ־ אִ֭ישׁ יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD desires certain things.
The LORD prefers righteousness and justice.
The LORD values righteousness and justice more than sacrifice.
Doing what is right and just pleases the LORD more than offering sacrifices.
passages.original: עֲ֭שֹׂה צְדָקָ֣ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט נִבְחָ֖ר לַיהוָ֣ה מִזָּֽבַח׃

passages.text: Haughty eyes and a proud heart— the guides of the wicked—are sin.
passages.sermon:
The wicked have haughty eyes.
The wicked have a proud heart.
Haughty eyes and a proud heart guide the wicked.
These things are sin.
passages.original: רוּם־ עֵ֭ינַיִם וּרְחַב־ לֵ֑ב נִ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃

passages.text: The plans of the diligent bring plenty, as surely as haste leads to poverty.
passages.sermon:
A diligent person makes careful plans.
These plans bring plenty.
A hasty person acts quickly without planning.
Haste leads to poverty.
passages.original: מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת חָ֭רוּץ אַךְ־ לְמוֹתָ֑ר וְכָל־ אָ֝֗ץ אַךְ־ לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Making a fortune by a lying tongue is a vanishing mist, a deadly pursuit.
passages.sermon:
A person may try to gain wealth by lying.
This person uses false words to make money.
Such wealth disappears quickly.
It is like a mist that vanishes.
Those who seek wealth through lies chase after death.
passages.original: פֹּ֣עַל א֭וֹצָרוֹת בִּלְשׁ֣וֹן שָׁ֑קֶר הֶ֥בֶל נִ֝דָּ֗ף מְבַקְשֵׁי־ מָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away because they refuse to do what is just.
passages.sermon:
Wicked people act with violence.
Their violence destroys them.
They refuse to do what is right.
They do not practice justice.
Their own actions bring their downfall.
passages.original: שֹׁד־ רְשָׁעִ֥ים יְגוֹרֵ֑ם כִּ֥י מֵ֝אֲנ֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: The way of a guilty man is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
passages.sermon:
A guilty man walks a crooked path.
He does not act honestly.
An innocent man lives uprightly.
He acts with integrity.
passages.original: הֲפַכְפַּ֬ךְ דֶּ֣רֶךְ אִ֣ישׁ וָזָ֑ר וְ֝זַ֗ךְ יָשָׁ֥ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
passages.sermon:
A quarrelsome wife causes strife in the home.
It is better to live alone on the corner of a roof.
It is better than sharing a house with a quarrelsome wife.
Living with constant conflict is worse than living in isolation.
passages.original: ט֗וֹב לָשֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־ פִּנַּת־ גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃

passages.text: The soul of the wicked man craves evil; his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man desires evil in his heart.
He wants to do wrong things.
He does not show kindness to his neighbor.
He does not see his neighbor with favor.
He does not care for others.
passages.original: נֶ֣פֶשׁ רָ֭שָׁע אִוְּתָה־ רָ֑ע לֹא־ יֻחַ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֣יו רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; and when a wise man is instructed, he acquires knowledge.
passages.sermon:
A mocker is a person who scorns or ridicules others.
A simple person is someone who lacks understanding.
A wise man is someone who seeks and values instruction.
When someone punishes a mocker, the simple person learns wisdom.
When someone instructs a wise man, the wise man gains knowledge.
passages.original: בַּעְנָשׁ־ לֵ֭ץ יֶחְכַּם־ פֶּ֑תִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְ֝חָכָ֗ם יִקַּח־ דָּֽעַת׃

passages.text: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.
passages.sermon: The Righteous One acts with wisdom.\r\nHe looks at the house of the wicked.\r\nHe brings the wicked to ruin.
passages.original: מַשְׂכִּ֣יל צַ֭דִּיק לְבֵ֣ית רָשָׁ֑ע מְסַלֵּ֖ף רְשָׁעִ֣ים לָרָֽע׃

passages.text: Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, he too shall cry out and receive no answer.
passages.sermon:
A person may hear the cry of the poor.
This person chooses to shut his ears.
He ignores the plea of the poor.
Later, this same person will cry out for help.
No one will answer him.
He will not receive a response.
passages.original: אֹטֵ֣ם אָ֭זְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת־ דָּ֑ל גַּֽם־ ה֥וּא יִ֝קְרָ֗א וְלֹ֣א יֵעָנֶֽה׃

passages.text: A gift in secret soothes anger, and a covert bribe pacifies great wrath.
passages.sermon: A secret gift calms anger.\r\nA hidden bribe quiets strong wrath.
passages.original: מַתָּ֣ן בַּ֭סֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה־ אָ֑ף וְשֹׁ֥חַד בַּ֝חֵ֗ק חֵמָ֥ה עַזָּֽה׃

passages.text: Justice executed is a joy to the righteous, but a terror to the workers of iniquity.
passages.sermon:
The righteous love justice.
Justice brings joy to the righteous.
Workers of iniquity do evil deeds.
Justice brings terror to the workers of iniquity.
passages.original: שִׂמְחָ֣ה לַ֭צַּדִּיק עֲשׂ֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝מְחִתָּ֗ה לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: The man who strays from the path of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.
passages.sermon:
A man can leave the path of understanding.
This man does not follow wisdom.
He goes his own way.
He will not find life.
He will rest among the dead.
He will join those who have no hope.
passages.original: אָדָ֗ם תּ֭וֹעֶה מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל רְפָאִ֣ים יָנֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: He who loves pleasure will become poor; the one who loves wine and oil will never be rich.
passages.sermon:
A man who lacks wealth loves pleasure.
He loves wine.
He loves oil.
He will not become rich.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ מַ֭חְסוֹר אֹהֵ֣ב שִׂמְחָ֑ה אֹהֵ֥ב יַֽיִן־ וָ֝שֶׁ֗מֶן לֹ֣א יַעֲשִֽׁיר׃

passages.text: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the faithless for the upright.
passages.sermon: The wicked pay the price for the righteous.\r\nThe faithless take the place of the upright.
passages.original: כֹּ֣פֶר לַצַּדִּ֣יק רָשָׁ֑ע וְתַ֖חַת יְשָׁרִ֣ים בּוֹגֵֽד׃

passages.text: Better to live in the desert than with a contentious and ill-tempered wife.
passages.sermon:
A man may have a wife who is contentious and ill-tempered.
A contentious wife argues often.
An ill-tempered wife becomes angry easily.
It is better for a man to live in the desert.
The desert is lonely and harsh.
Living in the desert is better than living with a contentious and ill-tempered wife.
passages.original: ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת בְּאֶֽרֶץ־ מִדְבָּ֑ר מֵאֵ֖שֶׁת מְדוֹנִים וָכָֽעַס׃

passages.text: Precious treasures and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man consumes them.
passages.sermon:
A wise person lives in a house.
This house contains precious treasures.
This house also contains oil.
A foolish person consumes these treasures.
A foolish person uses up the oil.
passages.original: אוֹצָ֤ר׀ נֶחְמָ֣ד וָ֭שֶׁמֶן בִּנְוֵ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וּכְסִ֖יל אָדָ֣ם יְבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor.
passages.sermon:
A person can choose to pursue righteousness.
A person can also choose to pursue loving devotion.
This person will find life.
This person will find righteousness.
This person will find honor.
passages.original: רֹ֭דֵף צְדָקָ֣ה וָחָ֑סֶד יִמְצָ֥א חַ֝יִּ֗ים צְדָקָ֥ה וְכָבֽוֹד׃

passages.text: A wise man scales the city of the mighty and pulls down the stronghold in which they trust.
passages.sermon:
A wise man acts with understanding.
He climbs up to the city where strong warriors live.
He enters the city of the mighty.
He brings down the strong place where they feel safe.
He destroys the stronghold that gives them confidence.
passages.original: עִ֣יר גִּ֭בֹּרִים עָלָ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗רֶד עֹ֣ז מִבְטֶחָֽה׃

passages.text: He who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from distress.
passages.sermon:
A person can guard his mouth.
He can also guard his tongue.
This person keeps his soul safe from trouble.
He avoids distress by watching his words.
passages.original: שֹׁמֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו וּלְשׁוֹנ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֖ר מִצָּר֣וֹת נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: Mocker is the name of the proud and arrogant man— of him who acts with excessive pride.
passages.sermon:
A proud man acts with arrogance.
He is also an arrogant man.
People call him a mocker.
He acts with excessive pride.
passages.original: זֵ֣ד יָ֭הִיר לֵ֣ץ שְׁמ֑וֹ ע֝וֹשֶׂ֗ה בְּעֶבְרַ֥ת זָדֽוֹן׃

passages.text: The craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work.
passages.sermon:
A slacker is a person who avoids work.
A slacker has strong cravings.
These cravings harm him.
His cravings can destroy him.
His hands refuse to work.
He does not act.
Because he does not work, his cravings lead to his downfall.
passages.original: תַּאֲוַ֣ת עָצֵ֣ל תְּמִיתֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־ מֵאֲנ֖וּ יָדָ֣יו לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃

passages.text: All day long he covets more, but the righteous give without restraint.
passages.sermon:
A wicked or lazy man always wants more.
He spends the whole day craving things.
He never feels satisfied.
A righteous man acts differently.
The righteous man gives freely.
He does not hold back when he gives.
passages.original: כָּל־ הַ֭יּוֹם הִתְאַוָּ֣ה תַאֲוָ֑ה וְצַדִּ֥יק יִ֝תֵּ֗ן וְלֹ֣א יַחְשֹֽׂךְ׃

passages.text: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable— how much more so when brought with ill intent!
passages.sermon: A wicked person offers a sacrifice.\r\nGod finds this sacrifice detestable.\r\nIf the wicked person brings the sacrifice with evil intent, it is even more detestable to God.
passages.original: זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָ֑ה אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־ בְזִמָּ֥ה יְבִיאֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: A lying witness will perish, but the man who listens to truth will speak forever.
passages.sermon:
A lying witness will perish.
A lying witness does not last.
A man who listens to truth will speak forever.
A man who hears truth will always have words to say.
passages.original: עֵד־ כְּזָבִ֥ים יֹאבֵ֑ד וְאִ֥ישׁ שׁוֹמֵעַ לָנֶ֥צַח יְדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright man makes his way sure.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man acts boldly.
He hardens his face.
He shows no shame.
An upright man acts differently.
He prepares his way carefully.
He makes his path secure.
passages.original: הֵעֵ֬ז אִ֣ישׁ רָשָׁ֣ע בְּפָנָ֑יו וְ֝יָשָׁ֗ר ה֤וּא׀ יָכִין דְּרָכָיו׃

passages.text: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is all-powerful.
No wisdom can stand against the LORD.
No understanding can overcome the LORD.
No counsel can succeed against the LORD.
passages.original: אֵ֣ין חָ֭כְמָה וְאֵ֣ין תְּבוּנָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין עֵ֝צָ֗ה לְנֶ֣גֶד יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A horse is ready for battle.
People prepare the horse for war.
The LORD gives victory.
Victory comes from the LORD, not from the horse.
passages.original: ס֗וּס מ֭וּכָן לְי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְ֝לַֽיהוָ֗ה הַתְּשׁוּעָֽה׃
